experience.title: Web Developer
experience.location: 212 Cottage Grove Suite A, Santa Barbara, CA 93101
experience.description:
Lead developer for an online benefits enrollment service.  Much like "Obama Care"​ or "California Care", we provided easy and seamless benefit management solutions to many large companies and non-profits.  My challenges at this company were to perform application penetration and patching, add new functionality to meet business requirements, reporting, mysql database management, query optimization, automated load testing, cross browser support, cross browser support for printing, design user experiences, data migration, single sign-on, automated testing, and everything that comes with programming on the LAMP stack and the browser front end.  I updated and modernized the user interface with jquery, blueimp, fusion charts, pdf downloads of reports, and optimized code to make the user experience excellent. 
I have 8 years of LAMP stack development using a custom MVC framework I created.  I also did some .NET programming for a client.

experience.title: lead programmer
experience.description: My primary responsibilities included:  web page data mining, LAMP stack web development, data verification, web design, action script programming, and front end development.  This company is no longer around but basically it was like the yellow pages but online.

experience.title: Lead Research Assistant
experience.company: California State University, Fresno Linguistics Department
experience.description: Working under a National Science Foundation (NSF) Grant and under the supervision of Dr. William Lewis I was tasked with extending his web-crawlers (written in Java) to utilize the Google and Yahoo search engine APIs.  I quickly integrated the the search engine APIs and further enhanced functionality by adding a mysql database, multi-threading, and other features that greatly enhanced the data mining capability of the program.  For example, if any of the threads were to error out then a new thread would be created and continue where the last thread had died.  The implementation of multi-threading turned a program that would crash every 3 days into a program that would almost never crash.  My program was also responsible for converting pdf documents into plain text documents and then extract any useful data.  I would later write an online data verification program where students in the Linguistics Department could verify the data collected.  I was the primary architect for the database schema.

volunteering-experiences.title: Board Member, Bicycle Mechanic, Cycling Instructor, Shop Volunteer
volunteering-experiences.subtitle: Santa Barbara Bicycle Coalition
volunteering-experiences.caption: Jun 2010 - Oct 2015 · 5 yrs 5 mos
volunteering-experiences.description: When I first learned about the Santa Barbara Bicycle Coalition I only cared to take their courses so that I could fix my bicycle.  After completing the course, I started volunteering so I could further increase my bicycle mechanic skills, but I was roped into volunteering on their open shop days where I would help the general public with their bicycles.  After several months I was asked to sit on the Board of Directors, and from there I became a certified instructor.  Initially I had only wanted to save a few bucks by fixing my own bicycle, but quickly became a core member of the organization and am a better person for it.
